issues.description: The problem UML specifies StockIngredient.price as an int, but the template StockIngredient class defines price as a double. This attribute type mismatch (int vs double) can confuse students about the expected type and causes inconsistencies with the UML and the solution, which uses int for price. Students following the template might implement logic expecting double while the exercises/tests and UML expect int.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the StockIngredient.price type consistent with the problem UML and solution by changing the template StockIngredient.price from double to int. Update the field declaration, the constructor parameter type, and the getPrice() return type in the template to use int.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML indicate the StockIngredient constructor signature is StockIngredient(String, int, int), but the template defines the constructor as StockIngredient(String, double, int). This constructor parameter mismatch (double vs int for price) will prevent students from matching the specified API and confuses them about what parameter types to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template StockIngredient constructor to accept an int for the price parameter (StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity)) to match the UML and the solution. Also ensure any usages in the template or exercises (e.g., acceptSupplyDelivery) expect an int price.
